title: ACME on-prem: day 3 install notes (scratchpad)
content:
Day 3 onsite notes + quick TODOs (working scratchpad)

Summary
- Focus: finish cluster install for ACME (staging on-prem), enable private runtime, verify GPU inference path.
- Status: cluster up, runtime containers start but we hit two blockers (nvidia/cuda driver mismatch, and private registry auth flaps).

Environment quick facts (customer)
- 3-node K8s cluster (kubeadm): 3 control-plane + 6 worker GPUs planned; currently 3 workers (2x A100, 1x A30)
- OS: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (custom image), kernel 5.19
- Container runtime: containerd 1.7.2
- Private registry: registry.acme.corp (self-signed certs)
- Internal KMS: Vault (transit) behind internal ALB
- Network: VPC-like VLANs, restricted egress, outbound to our telemetry endpoints blocked by default

What I ran today (commands / quick outputs)
- kubeadm join -> nodes joined cleanly, taints applied for gpu nodes
- containerd config tweak: set SystemdCgroup = true (we need systemd slice for runtime)
- installed nvidia driver 525.105.17 -> runtime pod logs show: "CUDA driver version is insufficient for CUDA runtime version" on A100 nodes
  - quick fix: bumped driver to 530.41.03 (matches CUDA 12.1 runtime in our image). Rebooted nodes, pods started to allocate GPUs.
- registry auth: initial docker login failing intermittently with 401. Debugging found an expired service account token on the registry side (ACME ops rotated tokens last night). Worked with Miguel to update robot account in /etc/containerd/certs.d and restarted containerd.

Runtime / Redwood-specific notes
- Deployed redwood-private-runtime:v2.4.1 -> uses /opt/redwood/bin/launcher systemd unit in container. Verified systemd unit config in image (escape hanged on PID1 previously).
- KV cache mount: we mount hostpath /mnt/redwood-kv -> Ensure ext4 mount with noatime and tuned read_ahead 4096 for better small-read latency.
- Telemetry: ACME policy blocks outbound metrics by default. We set TELEMETRY_MODE=disabled in runtime config; flagged for legal sign-off.
- License: customer will provide license.pem, drop into /etc/redwood/license.pem, restart runtime. Confirmed sample license accepted (tested with trial).

Blockers (current)
1) KMS integration flaky for vault-transit wrap/unwrap (intermittent 500 from Vault). Possible root causes:
   - Vault HA not fully healthy (leader flapping) -> ACME ops investigating.
   - Time skew between runtime nodes and Vault (NTP drift). Quick mitigation: force NTP sync on nodes, added note to ops run.
2) Private registry auth rotation caused container pull failures. Mitigation done but ask ACME to add robot account rotation procedure to runbook.
3) SELinux in permissive vs disabled: some nodes had SELinux enabled (per company baseline). Our container images expect permissive/disabled; left note to ACME to set SELinux=permissive for now.

Short-term checklist (what I need to finish)
- [ ] Validate GPU allocations across mixed GPU types (A100/A30) for model scheduling (Samira) - target EOD 2026-03-08
- [ ] Confirm Vault leader stability + rotate transit key (ACME ops + Miguel) - pending
- [ ] Add robot-account rotation docs to ACME runbook (Riley) - prepare PR against Confluence
- [ ] Run full e2e inference test (small prompt set) with telemetry disabled and capture latencies (Samira)
- [ ] Upload license.pem & verify license activation (ACME ops)
- [ ] Confirm RHN/kernel repo access for future driver updates (ACME infra)

Observed flaky behaviours to monitor
- Containerd restart sometimes leaves orphaned GPU device nodes under /dev/nvidia* until reboot; workaround: systemd tmpfiles.d rule to clean stale nodes. File a follow-up study with infra team.
- When scaling up pods quickly, we observed ephemeral port exhaustion on host (docker ephemeral range default). Added sysctl tweak: net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range -> widen to 15000-61000 during load test.

Notes for handoff / next onsite
- Bring USB with driver packages + offline registry mirror (for air-gapped install)
- Prepare a short slide deck for ACME ops on: driver strategy, container runtime config, license lifecycle, and KMS failover plan
- Ask infra to whitelist our troubleshooting jumpbox IP: 18.205.76.54 (temporary)

Random reminders / quick TODOs (personal)
- Ping legal about telemetry mode wording in contract (Samira)
- Update internal runbook template: add section for private-registry cert rotation and robot accounts
- Save failing pod logs to S3 (sensitive: use internal bucket redwood-private-deploy-logs)

Appendix - error snippets (copied)
- Pod log: "RuntimeError: cuda driver version 525 detected, required >= 530"
- Vault error: "500 internal server error - leader not ready"
- Containerd: "401 unauthorized: certificate signed by unknown authority" (registry cert self-signed)

Contact list

- ACME infra: Priya Singh (pri@acme.corp)
- On-call infra: Miguel Torres (miguel@redwood.ai)
- PM: Riley Nguyen (riley@redwood.ai)

If anything changes midday I'll append here. This is a scratchpad — not final customer doc.
